full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This Rule has been obtained upon an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashing of the proceedings of Nari-O-Shisu Case No.20 of 1997 (arising out of Mollahat PS Case No.8 21-11-1996 corresponding GR Case No. 809 of 1996) of the Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Daman Bishes Adalat No.2, Bagerhat, hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal. 

 3. On receipt of the FIR Mollahat PS Case No. 8 dated 21-11-1996 was started under sections 9(kha) and 14 of the Act 

 5. In due course the case was received by the Tribunal constituted under the Act. The accused petitioners appeared before the Tribunal and obtained bail therefrom. The Tribunal framed charge on 1-6-1997 against the accused petitioners under sections 9(kha) and 14 of the Act 

 7. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that facts stated in the FIR and in the police report and that facts stating which charge under sections 9(kha) and 14 of the Act as has been framed by the Tribunal do not disclose and constitute any offence under the provisions of law hereinbefore mentioned, the charges so framed are misconceived and illegal and that continuation of Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Case No. 20 of1997 of the Court of Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Daman Bishesh Adalat No. 2, Bagerhat would amount to harassment of the petitioners as well as abuse of the process of the court and, as such, the charges that have been framed by the order No. 17 dated 1-6-1997 and that the proceedings of the Case No. 20 of 1997 are liable to be quashed. 

 9. It is the prosecution case that petitioner No.1 along with his companions attempted to kidnap the informant Nargis Parvin to marry her against her will but she was rescued by the police of Mollahat Police Station from the place of occurrence i.e. from the house of Akbar Hossain, son of Dhala Chowkider of village Garfa PS Mollahat District Bagerhat. The Tribunal has framed charge against the petitioner No.1 under section 9(kha) of the Act i.e. to compel a woman to marry a person against her will and that against the petitioner Nos. 2-4 under section 14 of the Act i.e. for instigating the petitioner No.1 in the commission of offence under section 9(kha) of the Act and that because of said instigation offence under the said section 9(kha) of the Act was committed. 

 10. Allegation against the petitioner No. 1 is that he along with his companions tried to kidnap the informant to marry her against her will. Admittedly; informant could not be kidnapped because of intervention of police. It appears that an attempt was made by the petitioner No. 1 and his companions to kidnap the informant for compelling her to marry the petitioner No. 1 against her will but the informant could not be kidnapped since the police appeared at the place wherefrom she was allegedly about to be kidnapped and that she was rescued by the police of Mollahat Police Station. Sub-section 'kha' of section 9 of the Act provides for punishment of an accused in case of his compelling a woman to marry him against her will. It is apparent from the allegations made in the FIR, in the police report and that facts stating which charge has been framed, that the petitioner No. 1 neither had kidnapped the informant which of course has not been made an offence under section 9(kha) of the Act nor had compelled the informant to marry him or any other person against her will. This being the position, framing of charge against the petitioner No. 1 under section 9(kha) of the Act is not a legal one or, in other words, charge so framed against the petitioner No. 1 is not sustainable in law. 

 14. From the provision of the Act it is not seen that making of attempt to commit one of the offences, except cases in sections 7 and 10(2) that have been enumerated in the Act has been made an offence and that punishment has been provided therefor. In section 14 of the Act provision has been made for punishing a person if he instigates another for the commission of anyone of the offences enumerated in the Act and that because of said instigation person so instigated has committed any one of the offences mentioned in the Act. In the instant case offence as has been provided in clause (kha) of section 9 of the Act has not been committed and that being so, a charge under section 14 of the Act against petitioner Nos. 2-4 as has been framed is, in our view, not legal. 

 15. We have already observed that allegations against the petitioner No. 1 was that he tried to or attempted to kidnap the informant to compel her to marry the petitioner No.1 against her will. Admittedly, the informant was not kidnapped. An offence under section 9(kha) of the Act has been made punishable in a case where kidnapping has been made for the purpose of compelling a woman to marry one against her will. In the instant case there was no kidnapping except an attempt to kidnap the informant but ultimately, there was no kidnapping because of intervention of police of Mollahat Police Station. The allegations of the informant is, that the petitioner No. 1 along with petitioner Nos. 2-4 tried to or attempted to kidnap her to compel her to marry the petitioner No. 1 against her will. Offence as provided in section 9(kha) of the Act has been made punishable in a case where there has been kidnapping. Since there was no kidnapping and consequent thereupon as informant was not compelled to marry the petitioner No. 1 against her will, no offence under the provision of section 9(kha) of the Act was committed by the petitioner No. 1 and, as such, framing of charge against the petitioner No.1 under the said provision of section 9 of the Act is not legal. 

 17. Petitioners in the background of the facts that have been alleged in the FIR and in the police report i.e. charge-sheet, might have committed an offence under some other penal law but not committed any offence either under section 9(kha) or section 14 of the Act. In the afore-state of the matter we are of the view that framing of charge against the petitioners under section 9(kha) and 14 of the Act is not legal and, as such, continuation of the proceedings of Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Bishesh Case No. 20 of 1997 of the Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Daman Bishes Adalat, No. 2 Bagerhat would amount to harassment to the petitioners and that also would amount to an abuse of the process of court. 

 18. In the afore-state of the matter the Rule is made absolute and the proceedings of Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Bishesh Case No. 20 of 1997 of the Nari-O-Shisu Nirjatan Daman Bishes Adalat No. 2, Bagerhat is quashed.
